channel.title: Chorley Council Transparency — AI DOGE
channel.description: Independent analysis of Chorley Borough Council spending and governance.

item.title: Pick Everard: Sole Civil Engineering Consultant at £154K
item.description: Pick Everard is the only supplier for civil engineering consultancy at Chorley — 2 contracts, £154K, zero competition. The only election council with identified service category monopolies. Was the specification written to exclude alternatives?

item.title: The Alderley Hotel: Same Hotel, Two Suppliers, 63 Payments
item.description: The Alderley Hotel appears as both 'THE ALDERLEY HOTEL' and 'ALDERLEY HOTEL' in Chorley's supplier records — 63 combined payments at 4.4-day intervals (£14K). If one hotel is split into two supplier records, how many other suppliers have duplicate identities hiding their true spend?

item.title: SUEZ and HAGS: 4 Contracts Each — Incumbent Advantage or Best Value?
item.description: SUEZ Recycling (£385K, 4 contracts) and HAGS SMP (£381K, 4 contracts) are Chorley's most frequent contract winners. Landscape Engineering won 2 contracts worth £538K. Are specifications written to favour incumbents, or do these companies genuinely offer the best value?

item.title: 0% Description Completeness: Chorley's Transparency Code Breach
item.description: Chorley publishes zero transaction descriptions — a statutory breach of Transparency Code 2015 Part 2. 1,409 transactions (£19.5M) have vague or empty descriptions. The 'System' department is 100% vague. Only Burnley shares this failure among Lancashire councils.

item.title: Dawson Group and Matchtech: £342K to Unregistered Suppliers
item.description: Dawson Group Environmental (£214K, 78 txns) and Matchtech (£128K, 81 txns) both score 40/100 on supplier risk with no Companies House registration. Both show rapid payment patterns and single-department concentration. Why is Chorley paying £342K to unverifiable entities?

item.title: 87 Contracts Published After Award: Chorley's Retrospective Transparency
item.description: 58% of Chorley's contracts (87 of 150) were published after their award date. The public cannot scrutinise procurement decisions that have already been made.

item.title: £29,966: The Contract at 99.9% of the Threshold
item.description: Bryan Lee Building Contracts received £29,965.65 for the Coronation Recreation Ground — just £34.35 below the £30,000 competitive tender threshold. 9 Chorley contracts fall between 86-99.9% of thresholds.

item.title: £1.2M on Procurement Services: Is Chorley Paying to Pay?
item.description: Bloom Procurement Services received £1.19M from Chorley — 6.7% of the council's £17.8M annual budget spent on a procurement intermediary. What savings has the council realised?
